description: Corrected Wimley-White interfacial partitioning analysis with the helix-formation term stated explicitly, comparing AP-64 modules with membrane-active references
code:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size":9,"axes.spines.top":False,"axes.spines.right":False})
# Wimley-White interfacial scale (White & Wimley 1998), charged forms at neutral pH.
# NOTE: this scale is for an UNFOLDED peptide at the interface. Helix formation at the
# interface contributes an additional ~ -0.4 kcal/mol per residue from backbone H-bond
# burial. Both columns are reported; the helix bonus is an explicit stated assumption.
WWI={'A':0.17,'R':0.81,'N':0.42,'D':1.23,'C':-0.24,'Q':0.58,'E':2.02,'G':0.01,'H':0.96,
     'I':-0.31,'L':-0.56,'K':0.99,'M':-0.23,'F':-1.13,'P':0.45,'S':0.13,'T':0.14,
     'W':-1.85,'Y':-0.94,'V':0.07}
HELIX_BONUS=-0.40
pep={
 "AP-64 full (64 aa)"            :"DDKPDKPDDKPDDSGKDPKPDFPKFLSLLGTEIIENAVEFILRSMSRSTGFMEFDDNEGKHSSK",
 "AP-64 acidic N-half (21 aa)"   :"DDKPDKPDDKPDDSGKDPKPD",
 "AP-64 C-half (43 aa)"          :"FPKFLSLLGTEIIENAVEFILRSMSRSTGFMEFDDNEGKHSSK",
 "AP-64 amphipathic window (18)" :"GTEIIENAVEFILRSMSR",
 "LL-37 (37 aa)"                 :"LLGDFFRKSKEKIGKEFKRIVQRIKDFLRNLVPRTES",
 "magainin-2 (23 aa)"            :"GIGKFLHSAKKFGKAFVGEIMNS",
 "cecropin-A (37 aa)"            :"KWKLFKKIEKVGQNIRDGIIKAGPAVAVVGQATQIAK",
 "DCD-1L (48 aa)"                :"SSLLEKGLDGAKKAVGGLGKLGKDAVEDLESVGKGAVHDVKDVLDSVL",
}
rows=[]
for k,s in pep.items():
    per=sum(WWI[r] for r in s)/len(s)
    rows.append(dict(peptide=k,L=len(s),
        dG_per_res_unfolded=round(per,3),
        dG_per_res_with_helix_bonus=round(per+HELIX_BONUS,3),
        dG_total_unfolded=round(per*len(s),2)))
t=pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Wimley-White INTERFACIAL partitioning, water -> zwitterionic POPC interface")
print("(positive = unfavourable for an unfolded peptide; all peptides here are positive)")
print(t.to_string(index=False))
t.to_csv("wimley_white_partitioning.csv",index=False)
print(f"""
Corrected reading:
 - No peptide in this set partitions favourably as an UNFOLDED chain; LL-37 is +0.347 and
   magainin-2 +0.142 per residue. Interfacial partitioning of these peptides depends on
   coupled helix formation (the ~{HELIX_BONUS} kcal/mol per residue backbone H-bond term).
 - AP-64's amphipathic window (+0.328) is in the same range as LL-37 (+0.347), cecropin-A
   (+0.265) and DCD-1L (+0.388). Its hydrophobic segment is therefore as interface-competent
   as those of membrane-active peptides.
 - Full-length AP-64 (+0.467) is the LEAST interface-competent peptide in the set, and the
   acidic N-half alone is +0.877 per residue, by far the worst value here. Asp (+1.23) and
   Glu (+2.02) dominate that penalty.
 - The Wimley-White scale carries no term for anionic bacterial lipid, so whatever
   partitioning the C-terminal segment achieves is driven by hydrophobicity and would not
   discriminate bacterial from zwitterionic host membranes.""")

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5,4.8))
y=np.arange(len(t))[::-1]
cols=["#c0392b" if "AP-64" in p else ("#e67e22" if "DCD" in p else "#2471a3") for p in t.peptide]
ax.barh(y,t.dG_per_res_unfolded,color=cols,edgecolor="k",lw=.3)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(t.peptide,fontsize=9)
ax.axvline(0,color="k",lw=.9)
ax.axvspan(0.24,0.40,color="#2471a3",alpha=.10)
ax.text(0.32,5.6,"range spanned by\nmembrane-active\nreferences",ha="center",fontsize=8,color="#1b4f72")
ax.set_xlabel("Wimley-White interfacial dG per residue, unfolded chain (kcal/mol)\nhigher = less able to partition into a bilayer interface")
ax.set_title("The acidic N-half is a strong anti-partitioning module; the C-terminal amphipathic\nsegment is as interface-competent as LL-37 and cecropin-A",
             loc="left",fontweight="bold",fontsize=10)
plt.show()
